source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-277152:The statistic for killing a creaking doesn't increment when breaking a creaking heart
source_meta._title: The statistics screen does not visually differentiate the creaking and creaking_transient entities

stor.environment: A fresh single-player Java Edition 24w40a world in the Overworld, with the Winter Drop experiment enabled. Use Creative mode with commands/cheats available as a practical way to obtain the experimental blocks and execute the report's commands. Keep the fresh world's default doMobSpawning gamerule enabled.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to make historical Java Edition snapshots available, and select snapshot 24w40a.
Use a newly created world so the player's mob-kill statistics do not contain results from earlier testing.
Enable the Winter Drop experiment while creating the world; the creaking, pale oak log, and creaking heart content in 24w40a is behind this experiment.

Use Creative mode and enable commands/cheats. Creative mode is not stated as a bug requirement, but it provides deterministic access to the required blocks, while commands/cheats are required for the supplied /summon, /time, and /damage commands.
Remain in the Overworld. No seed or coordinates are specified.
Leave the doMobSpawning gamerule at its fresh-world default value of true so the creaking heart can spawn its creaking.
Use an open, solid, approximately level area with free space around and above the planned three-block log-and-heart column.
The instructions name default keyboard and mouse inputs. If controls have been rebound, use the bound input for the same action.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft: Java Edition using snapshot 24w40a. At the title screen, verify that the displayed version is 24w40a before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Java Edition title screen is open and identifies the running version as 24w40a.

steps.action: Open the single-player world creation screen by selecting Singleplayer and then Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: Set the new world's game mode to Creative. Ensure commands are available; Creative single-player worlds normally provide command access, but enable Allow Commands/Cheats if the creation screen exposes a separate option.
steps.success_cue: The world is configured for Creative mode and will permit in-game commands.

steps.action: Open the world-creation options containing experimental features, normally More -> Experiments in this version.
steps.success_cue: The Experiments screen is visible and lists the available experimental feature toggles.

steps.action: Turn the Winter Drop experiment on. Confirm any warning that experimental features may make the world unstable, then return to the main world-creation screen.
steps.success_cue: Winter Drop is shown as enabled for the new world.

steps.action: Create the world and wait until terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the loaded Overworld, can move normally, and can execute commands.

steps.action: Locate a nearby open, solid, approximately level area. Choose a position with at least two empty blocks above the ground for a vertical pale-oak-log, creaking-heart, pale-oak-log column, plus unobstructed ground around it where an entity can appear.
steps.success_cue: A clear construction position and surrounding spawn area are available in loaded chunks.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory action, whose default key is E, and open the Search Items tab, normally represented by a compass icon.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open with an item search field available.

steps.action: Search for Pale Oak Log. Pick up a stack of the block and place it into an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine slots at the bottom of the inventory and gameplay screen.
steps.success_cue: At least two Pale Oak Logs are present in one of the player's hotbar slots.

steps.action: Clear or select all text in the Creative search field, search for Creaking Heart, and place one Creaking Heart into a different hotbar slot. Close the inventory using E or Esc.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed, and the hotbar contains both Pale Oak Logs and a Creaking Heart.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so the player is not holding a block while killing the first creaking. Select a hotbar slot with the corresponding number key or mouse wheel.
steps.success_cue: The active hotbar slot is empty and the player's hand is empty.

steps.action: Open in-game chat using the chat action, whose default key is T.
steps.success_cue: The chat command input field is open.

steps.action: Enter the report's summon command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and a command-spawned creaking exists at or immediately beside the player's position.

steps.action: Move approximately two or three blocks away from the summoned creaking, then turn toward it so it is visible and within melee reach when approached. Do not leave the area.
steps.success_cue: The command-spawned creaking is clearly visible and can be approached for a direct player attack.

steps.action: Approach within attack range, place the crosshair on the creaking, and use the attack action, whose default input is left-click, to kill it. A command- or spawn-egg-created creaking in this affected version has only one health point, so one direct player attack should be sufficient.
steps.success_cue: The creaking has entered its death/removal sequence as a result of the player's direct attack.

steps.action: Wait until the first creaking's death animation has finished and the entity is no longer present before constructing the heart setup.
steps.success_cue: The first creaking has completely disappeared, leaving no command-spawned creaking alive nearby.

steps.action: Return to the clear construction position and select the hotbar slot containing Pale Oak Logs.
steps.success_cue: Pale Oak Log is displayed as the item held in the player's hand.

steps.action: Place one Pale Oak Log on the chosen ground block by aiming at the ground's top face and using the place/use action, whose default input is right-click. Placing against a top face makes the log's axis vertical.
steps.success_cue: One upright Pale Oak Log occupies the bottom position of the planned three-block column.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Creaking Heart.
steps.success_cue: Creaking Heart is displayed as the item held in the player's hand.

steps.action: Aim at the top face of the bottom Pale Oak Log and place the Creaking Heart on top of it using the place/use action.
steps.success_cue: The Creaking Heart is directly above and touching the bottom Pale Oak Log.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing Pale Oak Logs again.
steps.success_cue: Pale Oak Log is displayed as the item held in the player's hand.

steps.action: Aim at the top face of the Creaking Heart and place a second Pale Oak Log on top using the place/use action. The result must be a vertical three-block column ordered Pale Oak Log, Creaking Heart, Pale Oak Log from bottom to top. All three blocks must be aligned along the same vertical axis.
steps.success_cue: A vertical log-heart-log column is complete, with the Creaking Heart directly between two vertically aligned Pale Oak Logs.

steps.action: Open in-game chat using the chat action, whose default key is T.
steps.success_cue: The chat command input field is open.

steps.action: Enter the report's time command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and the Overworld has changed to nighttime while the aligned heart structure remains loaded.

steps.action: Stand near the column without leaving the loaded area and wait for the active Creaking Heart to spawn a creaking. Keep the surrounding ground in view by slowly scanning the area, but do not break or replace any part of the column. Continue only after a creaking has visibly appeared nearby.
steps.success_cue: A heart-spawned creaking is visible near the aligned Creaking Heart structure.

steps.action: Open in-game chat using the chat action, whose default key is T. Do this while the heart-spawned creaking still exists.
steps.success_cue: The chat command input field is open and the heart-spawned creaking remains present.

steps.action: Enter the report's damage command exactly as written, including the leading slash, selector, entity identifier, damage amount, damage type, and source attribution, then press Enter. Execute it from in-game chat as the same player whose statistics will be inspected.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and targets the nearest minecraft:creaking_transient entity, with the executing player specified as the damage source.

steps.action: Wait until the targeted heart-spawned creaking finishes its death/removal sequence. Do not run another summon or damage command.
steps.success_cue: The targeted heart-spawned creaking is no longer present, and both kill actions have been completed once.

steps.action: Open the pause menu using the menu action, whose default key is Esc.
steps.success_cue: The pause menu is open.

steps.action: Select the Statistics button in the pause menu.
steps.success_cue: The Statistics screen is open and its statistics-category controls are visible.

steps.action: Select the Mobs category or tab in the Statistics screen.
steps.success_cue: The mob statistics list is open.

steps.action: Scroll through the mob statistics list until both entries corresponding to the two creaking entity types are simultaneously visible. Stop interacting as soon as the two Creaking-labeled statistic entries are in view.
steps.exact_input: mouse wheel or statistics-screen scroll control
steps.success_cue: The Mobs statistics screen is open with both Creaking statistic entries visible and ready for visual inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The player's Mobs statistics screen is open immediately after one player-attributed command-spawned creaking kill and one player-attributed creaking_transient kill, and both Creaking statistic entries are visible. Hand control to the observation subsystem without clicking, scrolling, closing the screen, or otherwise changing the displayed entries.
uncertainties: The report affects both 24w40a and 1.21.3. Snapshot 24w40a is recommended because it directly matches the report's requirement to enable the Winter Drop experiment and was the version current when the report was created.

The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode is used only as a deterministic implementation choice for obtaining Pale Oak Logs and a Creaking Heart; commands/cheats are necessary for the supplied commands.
No seed, coordinates, biome, or precise construction location is supplied. The report supports using any suitable loaded Overworld area.

The report says the Pale Oak Logs must be correctly aligned but does not describe the placement geometry. External version-relevant documentation establishes that the heart and both logs must share one axis; a vertical log-heart-log column is the simplest practical arrangement.

The exact delay and position at which the Creaking Heart spawns its creaking are not specified and may vary. The executor must wait for the entity itself to become visible rather than relying on a fixed delay.

The exact placement of the Experiments button within the 24w40a world-creation screen is not stated in the report; the More -> Experiments path is an operational UI inference. The essential report condition is that Winter Drop is enabled before world creation.

The report does not explicitly state the doMobSpawning gamerule, but a heart-spawned creaking requires mob spawning to remain enabled. A fresh world normally satisfies this without an additional command.
